recent_posts.title: Getting started with Yazi terminal file manager on Linux
recent_posts.summary: Yazi is a feature-rich, Rust-based terminal file manager that offers image and file previews, syntax highlighting, fuzzy search via fzf, ripgrep-powered content search, bulk rename, multi-tab interface, and zoxide integration. A wrapper shell function lets you cd into the last browsed directory on exit. Installation is covered for Arch Linux, Ubuntu (Snap), and generic binary installs, along with optional dependencies like ffmpeg, fd, and ripgrep that unlock its full capabilities.

recent_posts.title: LibreOffice Questions Whether Euro-Office is Truly Sovereign
recent_posts.summary: The Document Foundation (TDF), the nonprofit behind LibreOffice, is publicly questioning whether Euro-Office — a new European office suite forked from ONLYOFFICE by Nextcloud and IONOS — is truly sovereign. TDF's concern centers on document format: Euro-Office's launch materials emphasize Microsoft Office (OOXML) compatibility rather than committing to ODF (Open Document Format) as its native default. TDF argues that real digital sovereignty requires open formats like ODF, an ISO standard not controlled by any single company, rather than just self-hosting software that remains structurally tied to Microsoft's format decisions. Euro-Office has not responded to TDF's public inquiry, and the question carries legal weight given Germany's existing ODF mandate.

recent_posts.title: Copy Fail Linux kernel privilege escalation vulnerability explained
recent_posts.summary: A 9-year-old logic flaw in the Linux kernel (CVE-2026-31431, dubbed 'Copy Fail') allows any unprivileged local user to escalate to root using a 732-byte Python script. The bug lives in the kernel's cryptographic subsystem and corrupts 4 bytes of a file's in-memory copy without touching the on-disk file, bypassing integrity checks. It was patched in mainline on April 1 after responsible disclosure. Risk is highest for multi-tenant hosts, Kubernetes clusters, CI runners, and cloud environments where the page cache is shared across container boundaries. Desktop users with updated kernels face low risk. CISA has added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and ordered US federal agencies to patch by May 15. A temporary mitigation is blacklisting the algif_aead kernel module.

recent_posts.title: Netherlands launches self-hosted Forgejo platform for government source code
recent_posts.summary: The Netherlands is building a sovereign, self-hosted Git platform for government source code using Forgejo, a fully open source forge licensed under GPLv3+. GitHub was ruled out for being proprietary, and GitLab for its open-core model. The platform, code.overheid.nl, soft-launched on April 24, 2026, and is already hosting repositories from the Dutch Electoral Council, the Ministry of the Interior, and several municipalities. Still in pilot phase, it aims to reduce duplicate development across agencies and give the government full control over its infrastructure.

recent_posts.title: VS Code was silently adding Copilot as a git co-author on all commits
recent_posts.summary: VS Code quietly began adding a 'Co-authored-by: Copilot' trailer to git commits after a pull request in April changed the default value of the git.addAICoAuthor setting from 'off' to 'all'. This meant any user who hadn't manually configured the setting had Copilot credited in their git history — even on commits written entirely without AI assistance. The trailer also appeared when Copilot features were explicitly disabled, and was appended after commit finalization with no chance to review it. A VS Code team member acknowledged the mistake on Hacker News, apologized, and a fix reverting the default back to 'off' has been merged and is expected in VS Code 1.119.

recent_posts.title: A Free Open Source Mobile Dev Hackathon Is Coming to the Netherlands on May 16
recent_posts.summary: OS-SCi, a Netherlands-based FOSS education institution, is hosting the Lomiri Tech Meeting — a free two-day hackathon on May 16–17, 2026 in Tilburg. The event targets students interested in open source mobile development for Lomiri and Ubuntu Touch. Attendees will hear keynotes from Lomiri UI project leader Mike Gabriel and Erik Mols, who will announce a new Lomiri Bounty Program offering real-world incentives for contributing to the Ubuntu Touch ecosystem. All participants receive free copies of Lomiri App Development Level 1 and Level 2 books. The event includes hands-on app development sessions guided by experts and is open to students of all experience levels.

recent_posts.title: What Are Linux Mint HWE ISOs and Do You Actually Need One?
recent_posts.summary: Linux Mint has released HWE (Hardware Enablement) ISO images for Linux Mint 22.3, shipping with Linux kernel 6.17 instead of the standard 6.14. These are not new releases but alternative installation images designed for users with very new hardware that may not be supported by the older kernel. Existing Mint 22.3 users who are already up to date likely already have kernel 6.17 and don't need these ISOs. The HWE ISOs are primarily useful at install time for machines where the regular ISO fails to boot or install. Users with NVIDIA, Broadcom, or VirtualBox setups should be cautious, as proprietary modules can have compatibility issues on newer kernels. The Mint team plans to continue releasing updated HWE ISOs as newer kernels land, bridging the gap until Linux Mint 23 arrives in December 2026.

recent_posts.title: Ubuntu’s Official Flavour List Is Shrinking, And That’s Not a Bad Thing
recent_posts.summary: Ubuntu's official flavour count is shrinking with the 26.04 LTS release, and the author argues this is a healthy correction rather than a loss. The piece examines why maintaining official flavour status requires real engineering resources, QA participation, and sustained maintainership — not just community enthusiasm. Examples like Ubuntu MATE's leadership crisis, Lubuntu's reduced manpower, and Ubuntu Unity missing key milestones illustrate the strain. The argument is that a leaner, well-supported official flavour list better serves users and maintainers alike, while the broader Linux ecosystem still offers unlimited community remixes and spins.

recent_posts.title: Microsoft Marks 45 Years of DOS by Open-Sourcing Its Oldest-Known Source Code
recent_posts.summary: Microsoft has open-sourced the earliest known DOS source code on GitHub under the MIT license, marking the 45th anniversary of 86-DOS 1.00. The release includes the 86-DOS 1.00 kernel, PC-DOS 1.00 development snapshots, utilities like CHKDSK, and the original assembler. The code originated from physical printouts kept by Tim Paterson — the original author who wrote QDOS in 1980 — which historians had to scan and transcribe into compilable form. This continues a pattern of Microsoft releasing historical code, following MS-DOS 4.0 in 2024 and MS-DOS 1.25/2.0 in 2018.

recent_posts.title: FOSS Weekly #26.18: Ubuntu's AI Move, New Entry in Home Directory, New Ubuntu Terminal, Fedora 44 Release and More Linux Stuff
recent_posts.summary: A curated Linux and open source news roundup covering Fedora 44's release with Linux 6.19 and GNOME 50, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS 'Resolute Raccoon' launch, a new standard Projects directory coming to Linux home folders, Warp terminal going open source, Firefox 149 quietly shipping Brave's adblock-rust engine, a PyPI supply chain attack via a hijacked GitHub Actions workflow, and LVFS introducing download quotas for non-contributing vendors. Also includes tips on GSConnect, Konsole, Ubuntu password recovery, and highlights of community projects.
